questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis is confused, and the hands flap when held out. Which medicine helps?

options.text: Lactulose
A sedative
A high-protein shake
An opioid

questions.explanation: A is correct: lactulose pulls ammonia out through the stool. B: sedatives should be avoided. C is food, not a medicine, and doesn't clear ammonia. D is not taught for this and can add sedation.

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis takes lactulose. What is the stool goal?

options.text: One hard stool every two days
Two to three soft stools a day
Six or more watery stools a day
No stools until confusion clears

questions.explanation: B is correct: the goal is two to three soft stools a day. A and D are too few, so ammonia builds. C is too many and causes dehydration.

questions.stem: Which plan fits a client with cirrhosis and confusion from ammonia?

options.text: Restrict protein and give a sedative at night
Keep protein in the diet and avoid sedatives
Hold lactulose while the client is confused
Restrict all fluids

questions.explanation: B is correct: don't restrict protein, and avoid sedatives. A does both things the video says not to do. C stops the medicine that clears ammonia. D is not taught and risks dehydration.

questions.stem: A scarred liver can't do its four jobs. Which problems result? Select all that apply.

options.text: Confusion, from ammonia that isn't cleared
Bleeding, from too few clotting factors
Fluid in the belly, from low albumin and backed-up pressure
Yellow skin, from bilirubin that isn't cleared
Low calcium, from an inflamed pancreas

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: the four jobs are clearing ammonia, making clotting factors, making albumin, and clearing bilirubin. E is a pancreatitis problem, not a liver job.

questions.stem: A client with ascites is about to have a paracentesis. What should the nurse have the client do first?

options.text: Drink two glasses of water
Empty the bladder
Lie flat with legs raised
Walk for ten minutes

questions.explanation: B is correct: have the client empty their bladder, and check vital signs before and after. A, C, and D are not part of the preparation taught.

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis vomits blood. What does this most likely mean?

options.text: Expected effect of lactulose
Possible bleeding varices, an emergency
Mild gastritis to recheck tomorrow
Low albumin

questions.explanation: B is correct: the liver can't clot, so vomiting blood may mean bleeding varices, swollen veins in the esophagus. That's an emergency. A and C miss the danger. D causes ascites, not vomiting blood.

questions.stem: Which plan fits a client with fluid in the belly from cirrhosis?

options.text: Daily weight, belly measurement, and about 2 grams of sodium a day
Weekly weight and a high-sodium diet
Restrict protein and encourage salt
Measure belly size only when short of breath

questions.explanation: A is correct: a daily weight and belly measurement, plus a low-sodium diet, about 2 grams a day. B and C add sodium. D checks too rarely.

options.text: Flapping hands and confusion
Severe upper belly pain that bores through to the back, with lipase 3 or more times normal
Yellow skin with a slowly growing belly over months
A liver scarred slowly over many years

questions.explanation: B is correct: severe upper belly pain through to the back, and lipase three or more times normal. A, C, and D describe cirrhosis, which is chronic; pancreatitis is sudden.

questions.stem: Which are part of care for acute pancreatitis? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fluids into a vein, often lactated Ringer's
Pain control
A calcium check
Nothing by mouth at first, while vomiting or in severe pain
Restrict fluids to protect the heart
A high-fat meal right away

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: fluids, pain control, a calcium check because calcium can drop, and nothing by mouth at first. E is wrong: big fluid shifts can cause shock early. F is wrong: mild cases start low-fat eating as tolerated.

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis on lactulose has had six watery stools today and feels dizzy. What is the priority?

options.text: Give the next dose on time
Hold and clarify the next dose, check fluid status, and notify the provider
Start a low-protein diet
Double the next dose

questions.explanation: B is correct: six watery stools is too much; dehydration and low potassium can make confusion worse, so hold, clarify, and notify. A and D give more of what caused the problem. C: the video says don't restrict protein.
